summary: Radar for 2026-10-25, GLP-1 focus. This snapshot has no new regulatory approval in the US or UK. The "FDA approves Eli Lilly's weight-loss pill" headline that resurfaced on Oct 24 turned out to be Medical Economics' Apr 2 2026 item on orforglipron (Foundayo). Treat it as old news, not Lane C. The best openings are next-gen drug names that few channels cover, which is the pattern behind EloraTZP. (1) Efpeglenatide: Hanmi's once-weekly GLP-1, approved in Korea on Oct 8 2026 for chronic weight management. Phase 3 had 448 participants: 9.02% average weight loss vs 0.89% on placebo at 40 weeks. Launch is expected around the end of October (Korea Biomedical Review/Yonhap say Oct 29). I found no English YouTube explainers, so it's ideal for the 'What Is [new drug]?' test. (2) Retatrutide for kidneys: phase 2b TRANSCEND-CKD (HCPLive, Oct 22) showed UACR down 49.2% vs placebo at 24 weeks, with no change in measured GFR. QA notes already mention a '49.2%' number, so check this isn't a repeat of a Short from the last 14 days. (3) The retatrutide sleep-apnea Phase 3 (NEJM, Oct 20) is still spreading (Medical Xpress Oct 24) and stays strong if we haven't made a long-form yet. Gray-market retatrutide keeps accelerating (Futurism 'bodega' lab analysis Oct 24, News24 South Africa Oct 25, plus CBS earlier). Use it only as 'what's confirmed?' Shorts. Lane A search questions with steady US demand: Medicare's $50 GLP-1 Bridge during open enrollment, tirzepatide side effects, stopping, and the pill vs the shot. Seasonal hook: Halloween (Oct 31) and then Thanksgiving. Body-worry 'honest uncertainty' Shorts can use the new taste/smell coverage (absolute rates 0.37% vs 0.22%, observational). Rejected: GLP-1 microdosing (India Today Oct 25, Yahoo Oct 24) and the retatrutide 'research-grade sourcing' checklist.

candidates.topic: What is efpeglenatide? Korea's first homegrown GLP-1 for weight management (approved Oct 8 2026; launch expected around the end of October)
candidates.angle: 'New GLP-1 Drug Decoded' series (Lane C/pipeline explainer). What efpeglenatide is (a once-weekly GLP-1 receptor agonist, the same class as semaglutide), the Phase 3 result (448 Korean adults without diabetes, average 9.02% weight loss vs 0.89% placebo at 40 weeks, 75.1% lost at least 5%), its common side effects (diarrhea 17.6%, nausea 16.6%, indigestion 15.6%), and a dated status: approved only in Korea, not FDA- or MHRA-approved. Separate trials, not head-to-head, and no 'beat' frame. Close by pointing viewers to a prescriber about approved options. Never suggest getting it abroad.
candidates.why_now: A new named drug with fresh human Phase 3 data and almost no English-language video coverage. That is the EloraTZP pattern (499 views). Korea Biomedical Review/Yonhap report a launch around Oct 29, which creates a second news hook within 48 h.

evidence.signal: MFDS approval; Phase 3: 448 participants, 9.02% vs 0.89% at 40 weeks, GI side-effect rates

candidates.topic: Retatrutide and the kidneys: phase 2b TRANSCEND-CKD. Albuminuria down 49.2% vs placebo at 24 weeks in adults with BMI 27 or higher and chronic kidney disease
candidates.angle: 'New GLP-1 Drug Decoded': what albuminuria (UACR) is, and why lowering it matters for kidney health. Retatrutide lowered UACR by 49.2% vs placebo and reduced intraglomerular pressure and kidney fat, but measured GFR did not change at 24 weeks. Explain why that's an early marker, not proof of protection; the outcome proof will come from TRIUMPH-Outcomes, running to 2029. Population: BMI 27 or higher with CKD (eGFR 25–75), with or without type 2 diabetes. Investigational, BLA planned for Q1 2027 per Lilly. Check that no Short on it ran in the last 14 days (QA notes already cite a '49.2%').
candidates.why_now: Reported Oct 22 (HCPLive). Kidney coverage is still limited to clinician outlets, and retatrutide is our highest-peak drug name (253 views as a Short).

evidence.signal: TRANSCEND-CKD 24-week data: UACR −49.2% vs placebo, measured GFR unchanged
